questions.question: A constellation of the northern sky easily recognised by a group of five bright stars forming a slightly irregular ‘W’ is called:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cassiopeia**__**.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Cassiopeia A is a **supernova** remnant.
 
• It is notable for being the brightest astronomical radio source in the sky.
 
• It is the strongest radio source in the sky outside the solar system and was one of the first radio sources to be discovered, in** 1947**.
 
• The five brightest stars of Cassiopeia – **Alpha, Beta, Gamma, Delta, and Epsilon Cassiopeiae **– form the characteristic** W-shaped** asterism.
 
• Its brightest star is Alpha Cassiopeiae or **Shedar (Arabic for “breast”).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Informatio__**

 
• **Cygnus**

 
 
• Cygnus X-1, denoted as Cyg X-1, stands as a celestial marvel in the constellation Cygnus, recognized as the first galactic X-ray source widely acknowledged as a black hole. .
 
• Its discovery in 1971 marked a pivotal moment in astrophysics, and since then, it has continued to captivate researchers worldwide.
 
• It boasts a remarkable **X-ray flux density, reaching 2.3×10⁻²³ W/(m²⋅Hz) or 2.3×10³ jansky.**
 
• Cygnus is non-reusable and is designed to burn up upon re-entry into Earth's atmosphere after delivering cargo to the ISS.
 
 
 
• **Orion**
 
 
• Orion constellation is one of the **brightest and best-known constellations in the night sky**.
 
• It lies on the celestial equator.
 
• Orion has been known since ancient times.
 
• The constellation is** also known as the Hunter,** as it is associated with one in Greek mythology.
 
• It represents the mythical hunter Orion, who is often depicted in star maps as either facing the charge of Taurus, the bull. 
 
 
 
• **Ursa Major**
 
 
• The name "**;Ursa Major"** is Latin for "**Greater Bear,**" and its mythology can be traced back to several ancient cultures.
 
• In Greek mythology, Ursa Major is associated with the nymph **Callisto**, who was transformed into a bear and placed in the sky by Zeus.
 
• Ursa Major has been recognized and represented in various ways by different cultures, including** Native American, Hindu, and Chinese traditions.**
 
• The constellation is part of the family of constellations that includes **Ursa Minor, Draco, and Boötes.**
 
• Stars in Ursa Major are relatively close to Earth, and some of them are part of the Ursa Major Moving Group, a **cluster of stars **that share a common motion through space.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2abca754ac179cbd9170148ce52c47b5f5d497efa68410190edc141a60bf5eba.png]

questions.concept: Origin and evolution of Universe Solar system
questions.question: A _________________ is a cloud of dust and gas inside a galaxy.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**nebula**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **nebula** is a cloud of dust and gas inside a galaxy.
 
• Nebulae are often regions where new stars are being formed.
 
• They can be composed of hydrogen, helium, and other ionized gases.
 
• Some of the well-known nebulae include the Eagle Nebula, the Orion Nebula, and the Crab Nebula.
 
• Nebulae can be observed in various colors depending on the elements they contain and the types of radiation they emit.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The term "nebula" was originally used to describe any diffuse astronomical object, including galaxies beyond the Milky Way.
 
• Modern astronomy distinguishes between different types of nebulae, such as emission nebulae, reflection nebulae, and dark nebulae.
 
• Emission nebulae glow brightly due to the ionization of their gases by nearby high-energy stars.
 
• Reflection nebulae do not emit their own light but reflect the light of nearby stars.
 
• Dark nebulae are dense clouds of gas and dust that block the light from objects behind them.

questions.question: On which day of the year is the earth farthest from the sun, at a position called aphelion?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**4 July**__.

__
 
• Aphelion

 
 
• It is the point of Earth's orbit that is farthest from the Sun.
 
• When the earth reaches aphelion, the sun appears slightly smaller in the sky at any other time of year.
 
• The earth reaches aphelion only once a year.
 
• It happens near of 4th of July.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• Perihelion

 
 
• ​It is the point of the Earth's orbit that is nearest to the Sun.
 
• It happens near of 4th of January.
 
• The earth reaches perihelion only once a year
 
 
 
• Equinox
 
 
• It refers to a day with an equal duration of day and night.
 
• There are two equinoxes in a year:
 
 

 
• March 20( Vernal Equinox)
 
• September 22( Autumnal Equinox)

 
• Solstice

 
 
• ​It is the time of the year when the sun is farthest from the equatorial giving the long days or nights.
 
• It happens twice a year
 

 
 
• Summer Solstice ( June 21)
 
• Winter Solstice( December 22)

questions.concept: Origin and evolution of Universe Solar system
questions.question: ______ is no longer considered as a planet within Earth's Solar system.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pluto.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• In** 2006 the International Astronomical Union (IAU) redefined the planets **to be the bodies in space having the** following characteristics:**

 
 
• **It is in orbit around the Sun.**
 
• **It has sufficient mass to assume hydrostatic equilibrium (a nearly round shape).**
 
• **It has cleared the neighborhood around its orbit.**
 
 
 
• **Pluto **perfectly meets the** two of these criteria **but **fails to fulfill the third.**
 
• In all the billions of years it has lived there, it has** not managed to clear its neighborhood.**
 
• **Clearing the neighborhood means** that the **planet has become gravitationally dominant —** there are** **no other **bodies of comparable size **other than** **its **own satellites** or those otherwise under its gravitational influence, in its vicinity in space.
 
• There are some** **objects from the **Kuiper Belt** which is under the area of **Pluto's gravitational area **but the** gravitational pull is not strong enough to pull **these **objects towards Pluto. **
 
• **So** **from 2006 Pluto is considered a Dwarf Planet, not a planet.**

questions.concept: Origin and evolution of Universe Solar system
questions.question: _________ oblong orbit overlaps the orbit of Neptune.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pluto's**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pluto's** oblong orbit overlaps the orbit of Neptune.
 
• Pluto is classified as a dwarf planet in the Kuiper belt, a ring of bodies beyond Neptune.
 
• The orbit of Pluto is highly elliptical, taking it inside the orbit of Neptune for 20 years of its 248-year orbit around the Sun.
 
• This unique orbital characteristic means that at certain times, Pluto is closer to the Sun than Neptune.
 
• Despite this overlap, there is no risk of collision due to their respective orbital inclinations and resonance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pluto** was discovered by Clyde Tombaugh in 1930 and was originally classified as the ninth planet of the Solar System.
 
• In 2006, the International Astronomical Union (IAU) redefined the criteria for planet classification, and Pluto was reclassified as a dwarf planet.
 
• Pluto has five known moons: Charon, Styx, Nix, Kerberos, and Hydra.
 
• The New Horizons mission, launched by NASA, performed a flyby of Pluto in 2015, providing the most detailed images and data of the dwarf planet to date.
 
• Pluto's surface is composed of a mixture of frozen nitrogen, methane, and carbon monoxide ices.
 
• It has a thin atmosphere that expands when it is closer to the Sun and collapses as it moves farther away.

questions.question: Which of the following statements most accurately describes the planet Saturn?

options.text: Its cloud-like outer regions consist of methane in the gaseous form and ammonia in crystalline form.
Its surface is reddish in colour.
It is a gas giant made up mostly of hydrogen and helium and the density is less than that of water.
It was the seventh planet discovered in the Solar System.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It is a gas giant made up mostly of hydrogen and helium and the density is less than that of water.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Saturn is a** gas giant **composed primarily of** hydrogen and helium**, making it the least dense planet in the solar system.
 
• It is renowned for its extensive and complex ring system, made up of** ice particles**, **rocky debris, **and** dust**.
 
• Saturn has at least **82 moons**, with **Titan being the largest** and the **second-largest moon in the solar system**.
 
• It possesses a strong** magnetic field,** which is influenced by its rapid rotation and metallic hydrogen interior.
 
• Saturn’s average** density is less than that of water**, meaning it would float if there were a large enough body of water.
 
• Saturn takes about **29.5 Earth years **to complete one orbit around the Sun, and it has a relatively short day, taking approximately **10.7 hours **to complete **one rotation** on its axis.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• The **seventh planet** discovered in the Solar System is** Uranus.** Uranus was discovered by **William Herschel in 1781.**
 
• It is the** third-largest** planet in our Solar System and is unique for its axis, which is tilted almost sideways.
 
• **Sun** The central star__ and the largest object in the Solar System, providing the necessary** heat and light.**

**Inner Planets (Terrestrial Planets):**

 
• **Mercury: **The smallest and closest planet to the Sun, with extreme temperatures.
 
• **Venus:** Similar in size to Earth but with a thick, toxic atmosphere and extreme heat.
 
• **Earth:** The only known planet to support life, with a diverse climate and water.
 
• **Mars**: Known as the Red Planet, with the largest volcano and canyon in the Solar System.

**Outer Planets (Gas Giants and Ice Giants)**

 
• **Jupiter:** The largest planet, with a strong magnetic field and many moons, including Ganymede, the largest moon in the Solar System.
 
• **Saturn: **Famous for its beautiful ring system and numerous moons.
 
• **Uranus**: An ice giant with a tilted rotational axis and faint rings
 
• **Neptune**: Another ice giant known for its strong winds and deep blue color.

 
• Asteroid Belt: A region between **Mars and Jupiter **filled with rocky debris and dwarf planets like Ceres.

questions.concept: Origin and evolution of Universe Solar system
questions.question: What do you call the point in the orbit of the moon or a satellite at which it is nearest to Earth?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Perigee**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• For the Moon or an artificial satellite body moving around the Earth in an elliptical orbit, the distance between the object and the Earth changes throughout the orbit.
 
• The Moon's orbit around Earth is elliptical.
 
• **The point of the orbit closest to Earth is called perigee, while the point farthest from Earth is known as apogee**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

__
 
• At the point of perigree in the orbit, the object is moving at its maximum speed (Kepler’s Second Law).
 
• An **apsis** is the farthest or nearest point in the orbit of a planetary body about its primary body.
 
 
• The Earth's two apsides are the farthest point- aphelion, and the nearest point- perihelion, of its orbit around the host Sun.
 
 
 
• **The point of maximum separation from the Earth is known as the apogee**. The apogee refers specifically to orbits around the Earth, and is equivalent to the apoapsis of a general orbit.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The terms** perihelion **and** aphelion** describe different points in our planet’s orbit of the Sun. This can also apply to other planets, comets, or bodies. 
 
• **Aphelion** is the point of the Earth’s orbit that is farthest away from the Sun. It always happens in early July, about two weeks after the June solstice, 
 
• **Perihelion** is the point of the Earth’s orbit that is nearest to the Sun. This always happens in early January, about two weeks after the December Solstice.
 
• The words come from Ancient Greek, in which** helios means “Sun,” apo means “far,” and peri means “close.”**

questions.concept: Origin and evolution of Universe Solar system
questions.question: Who was the first to develop a mathematical predictive heliocentric model of the solar system?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Nicolaus Copernicus.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Nicolaus Copernicus (1473 - 1543) was born in Kingdom of Poland.
 
• Nicolaus work **"De revolutionibus orbium coelestium" **(On the Revolutions of the Celestial Spheres), gives the information about heliocentric model.
 
• it provided information that **the Sun in centre of Universe and rotation of Planets around the sun**.
 
• It was **published in 1543,** the year of his death.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• I**mmanuel Kant (1724-1804) **is widely known for modern philosophy.
 
• His important work "**Critique of Practical Reason," **Kant discusses his theory of ethics, including the famous concept of the Categorical Imperative, which is a universal moral law.
 
• He also made contributions** to "Nebular Hypothesis,"** proposing that solar systems develop from rotating clouds of gas, anticipating later theories of stellar and planetary formation.
 
• **Galileo Galilei (1564 - 1642) **was Italain Mathematician, Physicist, and Astronomer
 
• Galileo is famous for his **improvements to the telescope**.
 
• He made contributions to the **study of motion and mechanics, the laws of falling bodies**.
 
• **Pierre Simon - Laplace (1749 - 1827): **was French Mathematician and Astronomer 
 
• He laid the **foundations of statistics and probability** theory.
 
• His work in mathematics led to the development of **Laplace's equation.**
 
• He also developed the **Laplace Nebular Hypothesis** independently of Kant.

questions.question: Which of the following planets is known as a gas giant?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jupiter.**__

__
 
• The gas giants of our solar system are **Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune**.

 
 
• These four large planets, also called **jovian planets after Jupiter, reside in the outer part of the solar system past the orbits of Mars and the asteroid belt.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• A gas giant is a large planet mostly composed of helium and/or hydrogen.
 
 
• These planets, like Jupiter and Saturn in our solar system, don't have hard surfaces and instead have swirling gases above a solid core.
 
 
 
• The planet is any of the large bodies that orbit the Sun, including Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune, in the order of closeness to the Sun.

questions.question: Which of the following planets does NOT have rings?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Venus**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Venus** is the planet that does NOT have rings.
 
• Saturn, Uranus, and Jupiter all have ring systems, though Saturn's rings are the most prominent and well-known.
 
• The ring systems of Uranus and Jupiter are fainter and less visible compared to Saturn's.
 
• Rings are composed of dust, rock, and ice particles orbiting around their respective planets.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Venus** is the second planet from the Sun and is similar in size and structure to Earth but has a thick, toxic atmosphere.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?

options.text: The size of Jupiter and Mars is similar.
The density of Saturn is similar to that of Earth.
The size of Earth and Venus is almost similar.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option** **4**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Earth and Venus are often referred to as "sister planets" due to their similar sizes, with Earth having a diameter of about 12,742 km and Venus around 12,104 km.
 
• Mars is not the warmest planet; Venus is the hottest due to its thick atmosphere that traps heat.
 
• Saturn has a much lower density than Earth. Saturn is the least dense planet in the solar system, with a density less than that of water.
 
• Jupiter is significantly larger than Mars; in fact, it is the largest planet in our solar system, while Mars is much smaller.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jupiter's diameter** is about 139,822 km, making it more than **6 **times larger than Earth.
 
• **Mars **has a **thin atmosphere** and average temperatures around -80 degrees Fahrenheit (-62 degrees Celsius), much colder than Earth.
 
• **Venus **has a dense atmosphere composed mainly of carbon dioxide, contributing to its **extreme greenhouse effect** and surface temperatures around 900 degrees Fahrenheit (475 degrees Celsius).
 
• **Saturn **is famous for its prominent** ring system**, which is made up of ice and rock particles ranging in size.
 
• While Earth is a rocky planet, both Venus and Mars are also terrestrial, but they differ significantly in terms of surface conditions and atmospheres.
 
• Earth has a stronger **gravitational pull** compared to Mars and Venus due to its larger mass, affecting the potential for retaining an atmosphere and sustaining life.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a moon of Jupiter?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Triton**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Triton** is not a moon of Jupiter.
 
• **Callisto**, **Ganymede**, and **Europa** are all moons of Jupiter.
 
• **Triton** is actually the largest moon of Neptune.
 
• Jupiter has numerous moons, with the four largest being the Galilean moons: **Io, Europa, Ganymede, and Callisto**.
 
• These moons were first observed by Galileo Galilei in 1610 and are some of the largest objects in our Solar System outside the Sun and the eight planets.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jupiter** is the largest planet in our Solar System and has a very strong magnetic field.
 
• Jupiter's atmosphere is primarily composed of hydrogen and helium, with traces of other gases.
 
• Jupiter's Great Red Spot is a giant storm that has been raging for hundreds of years.
 
• Jupiter's moons are of great interest to scientists because some of them, like Europa, may have subsurface oceans that could potentially harbor life.
 
• Neptune's moon **Triton** is unique because it has a retrograde orbit, meaning it orbits in the opposite direction to Neptune's rotation.

questions.question: Which star is also known as the ‘Pole Star’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The North star**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Polaris**, also known as the **North Star**, is the star located almost directly above the Earth's North Pole.
 
• It is part of the constellation **Ursa Minor** and is the brightest star in this constellation.
 
• The North Star is a crucial point of navigation in the Northern Hemisphere.
 
• Unlike other stars, Polaris appears to stay in a fixed position in the sky, making it a reliable point of reference for determining direction.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Polaris is actually a triple star system, consisting of the main star, Polaris A, and two smaller companions, Polaris B and Polaris Ab.
 
• The star is approximately **433 light-years** away from Earth.
 
• Due to its alignment with the Earth's rotational axis, Polaris has been used by navigators and explorers for centuries.
 
• In ancient times, Polaris was not always the Pole Star. The title shifts over millennia due to the precession of the Earth's axis.

questions.question: Which of the following planets’ atmosphere is made up of thick white and yellowish clouds of sulphuric acid?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Venus**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Venus** has a very thick atmosphere composed mainly of carbon dioxide, with clouds of sulfuric acid, making it the hottest planet in the Solar System.
 
• The atmosphere is so dense that it creates a runaway greenhouse effect, trapping heat and raising surface temperatures to around 465 degrees Celsius (869 degrees Fahrenheit).
 
• The thick clouds of sulfuric acid reflect sunlight, giving Venus its characteristic yellowish-white appearance when observed from space.
 
• The atmospheric pressure on Venus is approximately 92 times greater than Earth's, which is equivalent to the pressure found 900 meters (3,000 feet) underwater on Earth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Venus** is the second planet from the Sun and is similar in size and structure to Earth, earning it the nickname "Earth's twin."
 
• Despite its similarities to Earth, the conditions on Venus are extremely harsh and inhospitable.
 
• The planet rotates very slowly on its axis and in the opposite direction to most planets in the Solar System, including Earth.
 
• Venus has been explored by various spacecraft, including NASA's Magellan mission, which mapped the planet's surface using radar.
 
• Due to its thick cloud cover, the surface of Venus cannot be observed directly from space in visible light.

questions.question: Which of the following planets is considered as Earth’s twin planet?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Venus.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Venus**:-

 
 
• Venus is sometimes called Earth's twin because Venus and Earth are almost the same size, have about the same mass (they weigh about the same), and have a very similar composition (are made of the same material).
 
• They are also neighboring planets.
 
• However, Venus and Earth are also very different.
 
• Venus has an atmosphere that is about 100 times thicker than Earth's and has surface temperatures that are extremely hot.
 
• Venus does not have life or water oceans like Earth does.
 
• Venus also rotates backward compared to Earth and the other planets.

• Neptune:-

 
 
• It was discovered on the basis of the law of gravitation.
 
• It is the farthest known planet from the Sun in the Solar System.
 
• Its revolution period is 164 years and the rotation period is 16 hours and 7 minutes.
 
• Neptune and Uranus are the only two planets discovered with the help of a telescope.
 
 
 
• **Uranus**:-
 
 
• It is the seventh planet from the Sun and has the third-largest diameter in our solar system.
 
• It was the first planet found with the aid of a telescope, Uranus was discovered in 1781 by astronomer William Herschel, although he originally thought it was either a comet or a star.
 
 
 
• **Mars:-****​**
 
 
• Mars is called Red Planet.
 
• It has two satellites - Phobos and Deimos.
 
• Mars is the fourth planet in the solar system.
 
• It is the second smallest planet in the solar system.
 
• In English Mars carries the name of the Roman God of War.

questions.question: Which country launched the third ‘Long March-5', the largest carrier rocket of the country, in December 2019?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**China.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

 
• In December 2019, China launched the third **Long March-5,** the country's largest carrier rocket, from the **Wenchang Space Launch Centre in southern China's Hainan Province. **
 
• At **8:45 pm (Beijing time**), the rocket, coded as **Long March-5 Y3**, blasted off from the coastal launch centre carrying the **Shijian-20** science experiment satellite weighing over eight tons, the nation's heaviest and most advanced communications satellite.
 
• The satellite was sent into its targeted orbit about **2,220** seconds later.
 
• The Long March-5 is a massive two-stage rocket capable of carrying a payload of **25 tons,** equal to the weight of 16 cars, to low Earth orbit, 14 tons at geostationary orbit, eight tons at Earth-Moon orbit, or five tons at Earth-Mars orbit, more than twice the capacity of the existing main Long March series rockets.
 
• According to the China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation, the rocket is capable of sending probes to explore Jupiter and other planets in the solar system in tandem with an upper stage (CASC).
 
• The rocket is about **57 meters** in length, equal to a 20-story building's height, with a core stage 5 meters in diameter and four boosters 3.35 meters in diameter.
 
• The Long March-5 is much larger than the previous carrier rockets of China.
 
• It has a takeoff weight of around **870 tons** and a thrust of about 1,000 tons.
